content.jointProblem: Can uncertainty-aware policy-to-parcel matching and weather–satellite data fusion identify field-level hail exposure and potentially underpriced parts of Pannonia’s farm portfolio more reliably than municipality-level loading? The first experiment would test whether methods developed for crop monitoring transfer to hail-related losses, comparing location-linkage reliability and held-out loss prediction against the current baseline before proposing pricing integration.

rationale.text: Lekić has demonstrated field-level integration of satellite and meteorological data, providing a methodological starting point for exposure modelling rather than evidence of an existing hail model.

sources.quote: This paper presents a regression framework that combines seven Sentinel-2 derived spectral indices sampled at weekly intervals with ERA5-Land reanalysis variables

rationale.text: His parcel-boundary research directly addresses a component of field-level mapping in fragmented local agricultural landscapes, although it does not itself resolve settlement-only insurance addresses.

sources.quote: Accuracy was evaluated against 630 manually digitised parcels in a 5 000-hectare test region in the South Bačka district.
The method achieved an average boundary displacement error of 8.3 m and an over-segmentation rate of 14%

rationale.text: He has led agricultural data-fusion and modular pipeline development, with Python tooling produced by the project—relevant experience for moving beyond manual QGIS overlays.

sources.quote: Branislav Lekić led the work package on data fusion and model development
the design of a modular prediction pipeline.
The project produced open-source Python tooling for time series fusion

rationale.text: He has experience collecting agricultural ground truth with local cooperatives and translating research outputs for operational users.

sources.quote: worked directly with staff from three agricultural cooperatives to collect combine-harvester yield records and validate satellite-based estimates
gaining practical experience in translating research outputs into formats usable by field agronomists.

constraints.text: Field-level exposure assignment requires resolving or explicitly retaining uncertainty in settlement-only policy locations; a parcel map cannot by itself identify the insured asset.

sources.quote: a large share of our farm addresses are stored only at the settlement level, not as coordinates.

constraints.text: The available weather feed is daily and five-kilometre resolution. Any finer hail estimates must be validated rather than treated as measured field-level intensity.

sources.quote: We do receive daily gridded weather data from MeteoVoj d.o.o. at a five-kilometre resolution
a storm can devastate one village and leave the farm two kilometres away untouched.

constraints.text: Initial validation must be designed around the available three-year, approximately 1,200-policy dataset, with storm and year separation where feasible to avoid misleading validation from correlated losses.

sources.quote: We have three full claim years with geo-tagged loss data for about 1,200 farm policies to work with.

constraints.text: A usable deliverable must support automated pricing inputs and fit the existing Python quarterly batch workflow, rather than stop at a map.

sources.quote: turning that into something that feeds the pricing model automatically is beyond what our team can do alone.
Python-based batch scoring pipeline for quarterly rating factor refresh

constraints.text: The implementation and maintenance plan must accommodate shared operational staff and no dedicated company research unit.

sources.quote: The company has no dedicated research unit
a four-person pricing team and a six-person IT team who split their time between operational support and new product build.

constraints.text: The collaboration cannot assume Lekić remains at Novi Sad or controls BioSense resources: institutional participation and access must be re-established with his current institution and the BioSense group.

sources.quote: Left the University of Novi Sad in March 2026; now a postdoctoral researcher at a university in Austria.
Enquiries regarding ongoing collaboration or access to the CROPSENSE dataset should be directed to the Remote Sensing and GIS Group at BioSense Institute.

risks: The evidence concerns crop yield, vegetation monitoring and parcel mapping, not hail intensity estimation or insurance pricing. The first experiment must test this transfer explicitly; crop-damage signals may not represent hail intensity or building damage.
Daily five-kilometre weather data and ambiguous policy locations may not contain enough information to distinguish neighbouring farms, even after satellite fusion.
Cloud cover and satellite observation gaps may obscure short-lived hail damage. Published cloud-handling and SAR results for yield estimation do not validate hail-event detection.
Three claim years may contain too few independent hailstorms for stable generalisation. Loss amounts may also reflect coverage, asset values and claims handling rather than hazard alone.

The profile is stale and current availability is unknown. Although joint-project participation is marked open, the institutional move creates uncertainty about contracting, resource access and a University of Novi Sad collaboration route.

Budget, delivery dates, data-sharing permissions and deployment ownership are unknown. Integration could stall, as the company's earlier flood-mapping prototype was completed but not integrated into pricing.
questions: Can Lekić confirm current joint-project interest, availability and contracting institution, and can BioSense participate to establish the Novi Sad collaboration and any required resource access?
Which insured assets are in scope—standing crops, farm buildings or both—and can policies be linked to verified asset coordinates or parcel identifiers rather than only settlement names?

What hail-related variables, temporal aggregation, historical coverage, licensing rights and validation information does MeteoVoj provide? Are independent event observations, radar products or field inspections available?
Does the dataset include all exposed policies, including non-claims, policy periods, sums insured, deductibles, crop or building characteristics, event dates and cause-of-loss labels?

Can the first pilot use verified locations and independent hail evidence to test weather–satellite transfer, then assess settlement-location uncertainty separately, with storm/year-held-out comparisons against municipality loading?
What improvement and uncertainty thresholds would justify a pricing trial, and what explanation, actuarial approval, privacy and data-access requirements must outputs satisfy?
What budget, timeline and named pricing/IT maintenance owners are available, and which interfaces and infrastructure must the prototype support during any Guidewire migration?
